lead.title: A soybean line with 29 genes knocked out at once shows ultra-multiplex editing has arrived
lead.summary: A team reporting in Journal of Integrative Plant Biology built a modular Multiple SgRNA Array system that loads far more guides into one CRISPR/Cas9 construct without the vector instability and efficiency collapse that usually follow, validating 46 targets with 32 guides in hairy roots. They then used it in stable soybean transformation to knock out 29 genes across three modules at once, covering anti-nutritional factors, flavour compounds and nodulation, and recovered a line called rnp-29m carrying loss-of-function mutations in all 29. The mutant has higher oleic acid, fewer allergens and anti-nutrients, better digestibility and less beany flavour with no significant yield penalty, which is the kind of trait pyramiding conventional breeding cannot do. This is greenhouse and multi-generation screening work rather than field performance, so the yield claim still needs field trials.

notes.label: Plant science
notes.text: Regulators of grain and tuber quality dominate: an OsERF39 and OsNAC6 module keeps methylglyoxal in check during rice starch filling, StTCP6 trades potato branching against tuberisation through FLOWERING LOCUS T, and GmSUT4 links sucrose transport to root proton efflux under saline-alkaline stress in soybean.

notes.label: Biotech
notes.text: A strong day for editing tools: 29-gene multiplex editing in soybean, multiplex edits that break photoperiod sensitivity in tropical maize, the TAHITI transposon plus CRISPR system for targeted transgene insertion, and a Trends in Plant Science analysis across 47 species showing genome size and ploidy set CRISPR off-target potential.

notes.label: Prairies
notes.text: Prairie-relevant threads: a Canadian-led population genomic study of 84 Fusarium poae isolates in the cereal head blight complex, a new secreted chloroperoxidase behind Zymoseptoria tritici aggressiveness on resistant winter wheat, and a soybean haplotype map of 1,278 accessions that resolves cyst nematode resistance loci. Links to prairie fields are my inference; none was a Canadian field study.

plant.title: An OsERF39 and OsNAC6 module protects rice grain quality by clearing methylglyoxal
plant.summary: Methylglyoxal is a toxic byproduct of glycolysis and the Calvin cycle that builds up while rice grains fill with starch. The authors show that OsERF39 and OsNAC6 physically interact and together switch on OsGLYI7, a plastid glyoxalase I, and that knocking out any of the three cuts glyoxalase activity, lets methylglyoxal accumulate in leaves and endosperm, and disrupts redox balance. The mutants made less transitory and storage starch, accumulated less protein, and produced chalkier, lighter grain with reduced yield.

plant.title: A sucrose transporter and its partner let soybean roots acidify saline-alkaline soil
plant.summary: Overexpressing the soybean sucrose transporter GmSUT4 improved sucrose allocation to roots under saline-alkaline stress and cut electrolyte leakage and reactive oxygen species. X-ray computed tomography showed the overexpression lines built more root volume and surface area, and the extra sucrose coincided with more H+-ATPase transcript and protein, stronger proton efflux and greater root acidification. Interaction with GmCyt b5-2 boosted transport and proton efflux further, an effect lost in knockout lines. The work is physiological and molecular, with no field yield data.

plant.title: StTCP6 trades potato branching for tuber formation through florigen genes
plant.summary: The TCP transcription factor StTCP6 turns on the tuberigenic genes StSP3D and StSP6A and needs StSP6A to promote tuberisation, while also keeping axillary buds dormant to suppress shoot branching. Suppressing StTCP6 gave more branches, later maturity and higher yield, and overexpression did the reverse. Under long days, overexpression induced tubers in a short-day potato, which points to a lever for growing tuber crops outside their usual photoperiod.

plant.title: Rice grows two kinds of flooding root on separate developmental programs
plant.summary: Rice makes thin (AR1) and thick (AR2) adventitious roots when submerged, and this study shows they follow distinct paths before emergence, with AR1 taking longer and AR2 delayed but thickened by the enclosing leaf sheath through extra cortical cell layers and larger cortical cells. Comparative transcriptomes of nodal tissue identified OsWOX11 as the main driver of total root number, acting mostly through AR2. The coding sequence is conserved across accessions but the promoter varies, and a haplotype 3 promoter variant drove markedly higher activity than haplotype 1, flagged by the authors as a candidate resource for flooding resilience rather than a tested trait.

plant.title: A CaBIM1 and CaAP2/ERF142 pair builds lignin to protect pepper from cold
plant.summary: Pepper is cold sensitive, and the authors identify a complex of CaAP2/ERF142 and CaBIM1 that activates the lignin genes CaCAD1 and CaPAL directly. Silencing CaCAD1 or either regulator reduced lignin deposition, weakened membranes and impaired reactive oxygen species scavenging, worsening cold injury, while overexpressing CaAP2/ERF142 or CaBIM1 in tomato raised cold resistance. The functional tests used virus-induced gene silencing in pepper and transgenic tomato rather than field-grown pepper.

plant.title: A DNA repair helicase is needed for maize lateral roots and kernel size
plant.summary: The maize mutant dlr8-1 makes fewer lateral roots because cell proliferation falls, impairing both primordium initiation and later morphogenesis. ZmDLR8, also called ZmRTEL1, encodes a nuclear DNA helicase, and the mutation activates DNA damage responses and raises damage levels further when plants are treated with a DNA-damaging agent. The mutant was also shorter with smaller kernels and lower grain yield, tying genome maintenance in the root to yield components.

plant.title: Leaf infection reprograms roots within a day to build disease-suppressive soil
plant.summary: Foliar infection of Arabidopsis thaliana by Hyaloperonospora arabidopsidis is known to leave a soil legacy that protects the next generation, and a 7 day RNA-seq time course of roots grown in natural soil shows the reprogramming starts within 1 day. Salicylic acid defence genes went up and secondary metabolism and jasmonate genes went down, with salicylic acid rising at 1 day and jasmonate falling by 3 days, mostly in root tips. Mutant tests confirmed salicylic acid, jasmonate, indole glucosinolates, camalexin and flavonoids all contribute. This is an Arabidopsis-only system, so the crop relevance is untested.

plant.title: A cytokinin response regulator couples tomato growth to basal zinc uptake
plant.summary: Zinc deficiency suppresses cytokinin signalling in tomato, and this study runs the loop the other way by identifying SlRR26, a type-B response regulator downstream of cytokinin, as a regulator of zinc homeostasis in roots. Combining transcriptomes with DAP-seq showed it sits atop a network covering ion transport, metal binding, cell wall remodelling and hormone signalling, and it binds and activates the zinc transporter promoters SlZIP4 and SlZIP5. Zinc deficiency lowers SlRR26 while strongly inducing SlZIP4 and SlZIP5, so the stress response appears decoupled from the growth-coupled module.

plant.title: A wild wheat relative turns out to have an almost entirely rearranged karyotype
plant.summary: Triticeae chromosomes usually keep their colinearity across species, but fluorescence in situ hybridisation with a large probe set shows that in Aegilops uniaristata, a diploid wild wheat relative with the NN genome and 2n = 2x = 14, every chromosome except 5N is significantly rearranged by translocations and inversions relative to wheat. Having the macrostructure mapped matters for anyone trying to move N-genome segments into wheat, because rearrangements determine which introgressions will pair and recombine.

plant.title: Autophagy strips organelles out of maturing seeds
plant.summary: Using Arabidopsis thaliana seeds carrying organelle-specific fluorescent markers, the authors tracked plastids, endoplasmic reticulum, peroxisomes and mitochondria through maturation and found all of them rapidly reduced and remodelled as the seed moves into quiescence. Autophagy-defective mutants abnormally retained or accumulated organelles and organelle-derived material, showing autophagy drives the transition rather than merely accompanying it. The work is Arabidopsis-only, with implications for seed longevity and vigour in crops still to be tested.

biotech.title: An ultra-multiplex CRISPR system knocks out 29 soybean genes in one line
biotech.summary: The Multiple SgRNA Array system is a modular architecture that avoids the vector instability from repetitive Pol III promoters and the efficiency drop that comes with more guides, and hairy root assays showed it editing 46 targets with 32 guides at once. Deployed in stable soybean transformation, it knocked out 29 genes across anti-nutritional factor, flavour and nodulation modules, and multi-generation screening recovered the rnp-29m line with loss-of-function mutations in all 29. Seeds had more oleic acid, fewer allergens and anti-nutrients, better digestibility and weaker beany flavour, reported with no significant yield penalty in greenhouse-stage material.

biotech.title: Multiplex editing frees tropical maize from photoperiod sensitivity
biotech.summary: Tropical maize germplasm holds useful diversity but flowers too late under long days to be used directly in temperate breeding. This report describes multiplex genome editing to remove that photoperiod sensitivity, opening tropical lines to temperate programmes. Only the title and record were available through PubMed at the time of writing, with no abstract, so the editing targets and the size of the flowering-time shift could not be checked.

biotech.title: TAHITI pairs a crippled transposon with CRISPR for accurate transgene insertion
biotech.summary: Choosing where a transgene lands matters for expression, durability and later trait stacking, but targeted integration has been inefficient. The authors previously coupled the rice mPing and Pong transposon system to CRISPR-Cas but suffered high off-target mPing insertion, so here they engineer CRISPR-Cas to take over the DNA cleavage role from the Pong protein, immobilising the transposon. The result, Transposon-Assisted Homology-Independent Targeted Integration, gave higher on-target rates, fewer off-target insertions and smaller junction scars, improved further by removing one Pong protein, intronising coding regions and heat-shocking plants.

biotech.title: A soybean haplotype map of 1,278 accessions adds wild diversity back in
biotech.summary: GmHapMap-II comes from whole-genome sequencing of 1,278 Glycine max and Glycine soja accessions on a near-gapless reference, yielding 11.37 million SNPs and 2.05 million short insertions and deletions, and it breaks the diversity ceiling of the earlier cultivated-only map by including wild germplasm. Six geographically distinct subpopulations shaped linkage and recombination. The map sharpened the known chromosome 15 protein association and found a chromosome 1 locus for linolenic acid distinct from all known FAD3 genes, on a haplotype almost exclusive to wild G. soja, plus new haplotype and copy number structure at the cyst nematode loci rhg-1 and Rhg-4.

biotech.title: Less active deaminase variants make better cytosine base editors
biotech.summary: SsdA is among the smallest and most active cytosine deaminases used in base editors, but the wild-type protein is a bacterial toxin and unusable as a result. Comparing several modified versions, the authors found that amino acid substitutions at one key residue relieve toxicity through steric change, and that in vitro deaminase activity was negatively related to in vivo base editing performance, so the less active variants are the better tools. Homologues were similarly toxic, two were confirmed as cytosine deaminases, and one supported a new, highly functional editor.

biotech.title: Genome size and ploidy set how much off-target risk CRISPR carries in a crop
biotech.summary: Plant genome editing is widely treated as precise, but this analysis across 47 plant species finds that genome size and ploidy shape the predicted off-target landscape of CRISPR-Cas systems. The authors argue genome architecture belongs in the molecular characterisation of edited crops and in case-by-case regulatory evaluation, rather than assuming a single specificity standard across species. The off-target landscapes are computational predictions, not measured edits.

biotech.title: Review: engineering rhizobia to win the competition in real soil
biotech.summary: Rhizobial inoculants often fail because native soil strains outcompete them for nodule occupancy, the long-standing rhizobium competition problem. This review surveys synthetic biology routes to building competitiveness into elite strains through Nod factor biosynthesis, bacteriocin production, stress tolerance, motility and metabolism, and covers recent genome editing toolkits for diverse rhizobia. The authors stress that any genetic change has to be judged against the wider soil community rather than in pure culture. This is a review of prospects, not a field-tested inoculant.

biotech.title: Review: medical RNA delivery platforms do not transfer cleanly to crop protection
biotech.summary: Agricultural RNA research often assumes that lipid nanoparticles, polymeric carriers, extracellular vesicles and engineered nanomaterials developed for human medicine can be adapted directly to crops. This review challenges that, arguing the biological barriers are similar, including RNA degradation, poor uptake and limited intracellular release, but the constraints are not, because field use means open environmental exposure, plant-specific morphology, diffuse biodistribution and field-scale cost. It proposes a use-case framework classifying each carrier by transfer potential instead of hunting for one optimal carrier.

biotech.title: A fungal enzyme expressed in planta loosens the cell wall without weakening immunity
biotech.summary: Lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases help enzyme cocktails break down biomass in vitro, but their effect inside plants was unexplored. Expressing the fungal PcAA14 from Pycnoporus coccineus in Arabidopsis thaliana under constitutive and xylem-specific promoters raised cellulose and lowered lignin, and the walls released more glucose and xylose after cellulase and xylanase digestion. The lines showed no morphological or anatomical abnormality and were more resistant to Pseudomonas syringae with higher immunity marker expression. The result is Arabidopsis-only and has not been moved into a bioenergy crop.

biotech.title: A GRF and GIF fusion protein lifts jujube regeneration to 72.5%
biotech.summary: Poor in vitro regeneration blocks functional genomics in Chinese jujube, Ziziphus jujuba. Comparing single-gene overexpression with fusions, a ZjGRF3 and ZjGIF1 chimera promoted regeneration more than either gene alone, and mutating the miR396 target site raised regeneration efficiency to 72.51% and significantly improved transformation. All treatments gave 100% callus induction, so the gains came later, in adventitious shoot number per callus and faster shoot emergence.

ag.title: Twenty-nine years of GM crops cut pesticide active ingredient by 867 million kg
ag.summary: This global assessment of pesticide use change with herbicide-tolerant and insect-resistant crops from 1996 to 2024 puts the reduction at 866.9 million kg of active ingredient, or 6.5%, with a larger 15.3% fall in the Environmental Impact Quotient indicator. Insect-resistant cotton accounted for the biggest share at 427 million kg saved and a 29% drop in that crop's environmental impact score. The analysis comes from the long-running Brookes and Barfoot series and rests on modelled counterfactual pesticide use, so the totals depend on assumptions about what growers would otherwise have sprayed.

ag.title: Nationwide screen of 2,381 rice false smut isolates finds triazole resistance still rare
ag.summary: Resistance monitoring of 2,381 Ustilaginoidea virens isolates from 48 regions across 17 Chinese provinces and municipalities found only a handful of resistant isolates to four demethylation inhibitor fungicides: 0.21% for hexaconazole, 0.29% for epoxiconazole, 0.04% for propiconazole and 0.08% for difenoconazole, with Jiangxi and Jilin higher at 4.29% and 3.64%. Resistant isolates grew, sporulated and handled abiotic stress no differently, and showed cross-resistance only between epoxiconazole and propiconazole. No CYP51 or promoter mutations were found, but CYP51 was strongly overexpressed in resistant isolates under treatment.

ag.title: A secreted chloroperoxidase explains why some Septoria isolates push through resistant wheat
ag.summary: Quantitative resistance is the durable option in cereal breeding, but variation in pathogen aggressiveness can erode it. A pathogen-centred genome-wide association study of 131 Zymoseptoria tritici field isolates from the United Kingdom and Ireland on the resistant winter wheat KWS Extase found pycnidia density was continuously distributed, consistent with a quantitative trait rather than resistance breaking. One significant peak on chromosome 2 fine-mapped to ZtChp, a predicted secreted heme-binding chloroperoxidase conserved across fungi, and natural variants including a truncating frameshift were linked to reduced pycnidia formation.

ag.title: The fungicide-insensitive EU43 late blight lineage is no more virulent on resistance genes
ag.summary: The Phytophthora infestans lineage EU43, insensitive to mandipropamid, has raised alarm in European potato production, so the authors tested 28 isolates including 14 EU43 representatives against potato clones carrying single resistance genes. Lineage explained no significant difference in disease incidence, though individual isolates varied within lineages. Clones with Rpi-vnt1.1, Rpi-blb2 and R9a were consistently least diseased, while R3a and Rpi-blb3 were overcome more often. Leaf disc and whole-plant greenhouse assays agreed closely, with a concordance correlation coefficient of 0.983.

ag.title: Repeat-rich accessory regions drive genome evolution in a cryptic head blight fungus
ag.summary: Fusarium poae turns up constantly in Fusarium head blight pathosystems while causing few symptoms. Genomic analysis of 84 isolates, mostly a contemporary Canadian collection with international additions and including 12 long-read assemblies, showed genomes split into gene-dense core regions and repeat-rich accessory regions covering whole chromosomes and subtelomeric stretches. Accessory sequences were broadly shared but variably arranged, so discrete accessory chromosome identities could not be assigned consistently, and some accessory loci were unusually similar to sequences in F. langsethiae and F. oxysporum.

ag.title: Low tunnels paid back in about a year in New York strawberry trials
ag.summary: Three years of day-neutral strawberry field trials at Geneva, New York were combined with a one-acre economic model. Low tunnels raised total yield in two of three years and improved marketability in all three, lifting modelled marketable output from 14,414 to 23,784 pounds per acre and net operating profit from $13,250 to $35,393 per acre. Over five years the incremental net present value was about $79,121 per acre, a benefit-to-cost ratio of 3.93 and a 1.07 year payback, most sensitive to price, marketable yield response, packout and the cost of managing Tetranychus urticae.

ag.title: A spelt accession yields a powdery mildew gene and markers for selection
ag.summary: Spelt accession L251 resisted two powdery mildew isolates through a single dominant gene, which bulked segregant analysis and linkage mapping placed in a 2.52 Mb interval on chromosome arm 2BL between 701.81 and 704.33 Mb; sequence alignment showed it is the same as a previously described gene. Expression rose sixfold by 12 hours after inoculation in L251 and was undetectable in the susceptible line, and differentially expressed genes were enriched for fungal defence, oxidative stress, chitin catabolism and phenylpropanoid biosynthesis. Four linked markers were validated across 46 susceptible cultivars for marker-assisted selection.

ag.title: A sugar beet resistance protein recognises a region viruses cannot afford to change
ag.summary: Rhizomania control in sugar beet rests on Rz1, now widely broken, and Rz2, which has held. The authors show the Rz2 receptor recognises the triple gene block 1 protein from more viruses than previously known, including species that do not naturally infect beet, and that recognition depends on a C-terminal region carrying two conserved helicase motifs. Soil bait plant assays with naturally infected soils turned up no resistance-breaking mutations, and an artificial swap of four conserved residues escaped recognition but destroyed protein function, which is the authors' argument for durability.

ag.title: A Trichoderma strain cut wheat sharp eyespot incidence from 100% to 7.4%
ag.summary: Trichoderma asperellum NNIBRFG4324 inhibited mycelial growth of the soilborne wheat pathogen Ceratobasidium cereale by 71.1% in dual culture, and a cellophane membrane assay showed inhibition without direct contact. The strain showed chitinase-associated and cellulase activity in plate assays. In wheat seedlings, disease incidence fell from 100% in the pathogen-only treatment to 7.4%, a control efficacy of 92.6%, against 96.3% for the fungicide thifluzamide. These are controlled-environment seedling results, not field trials.

ag.title: Searchlight traps trace planthopper migration between Yunnan and Southeast Asia
ag.summary: High-altitude searchlight traps at Jiangcheng from 2021 to 2025 and Lancang from 2022 to 2024 caught brown planthopper and white-backed planthopper nearly year-round, with migration mainly from March to November and the white-backed species arriving about two weeks earlier and in greater numbers. Ovarian dissection classified 61.8% of 34 brown planthopper events as immigration and 38.2% as local emigration, and 29 of 48 white-backed events as immigration. HYSPLIT trajectories put spring immigrants mainly in Myanmar, summer arrivals in northern Thailand, Laos and Myanmar, and autumn arrivals in northern Laos and Vietnam.

methods: Coverage window: 15 to 17 November 2026 (about 48 hours; the previous issue was 2026-11-15, so nothing was skipped). Items were found through PubMed searches filtered on entry date (15 to 17 November) across plant science, biotechnology, genomics, pathology, entomology and pest management journals, and every date comes from the PubMed record because publisher and news sites were not reachable from this session: www.global-agriculture.com failed to resolve and would need to be allowed in the session's network settings. Web search surfaced two policy and industry threads I could not date-verify and therefore left out, a Defra clearance for a Phytoform bruise-resistant potato release in England reported as permitted on or after 19 November 2026, and a 4 November 2026 Bayer licence for University of California, Davis nitrogen-fixation editing technology; both would need the primary notice or release to confirm. Today's briefing is journal-only as a result. Two items carry only a month in PubMed (both Molecular Plant Pathology) and are dated to their 16 November entry; the jujube regeneration paper is dated 14 November by the journal but entered PubMed inside the window. Arabidopsis-only results (the soil-borne legacy root network, seed maturation autophagy and the lytic polysaccharide monooxygenase lines) are flagged, as are greenhouse, seedling and controlled-environment results without field data, modelled counterfactuals in the GM pesticide analysis, computational off-target predictions, and two reviews. The tropical maize editing paper had no abstract available, which is stated in its summary. No preprints or company claims are included. Items from the 12 to 15 November issues were skipped, including the Metarhizium plus resistant rice planthopper study and the perennial grass senescence atlas, as were catch-up records whose publication dates fall in August or October.
